title: Implement transparent admission-expiry to stop long-context request suffocation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Multiple customers (hosted and Dedicated) reported recurring high tail-latency events linked to sustained long-context requests. Root cause appears to be the continuous batcher holding admission slots indefinitely for long-sequence inflight requests, causing short requests to be starved (queue suffocation) during microburst windows. On Private deployments, upgrade windows and prefetch behavior amplified the effect due to slower eviction hysteresis.

Impact:
- Customer-facing escalations from three top-tier customers (chat product stalls, search reranking timeouts).
- SLO violations: p95 token latency spikes up to 3x for short and medium requests during mixed-length waves.
- Increased error budgets and emergency Dedicated capacity scaling for two enterprise tenants.

Repro steps (internal):
1) Use mixed workload generator: 80% short (<=64 tokens) chat requests, 20% long (>=8k tokens) sequences with steady arrival rate and occasional bursts.
2) Run on a single-medium serving pool that includes KV cache enabled and prefetch turned on.
3) Observe queue depth, admission queue wait times, and continuous-batcher occupancy.
4) Confirm short-request latencies climb while long requests stay healthy.

Investigation notes:
- The continuous batcher holds an admission token for a logical 'slot' until a long request finishes generating; admission tokens were not expiring when sequence generation exceeded expected boundaries.
- KV-cache eviction windows interact with admission lifetimes: eviction-induced cache misses on long requests can extend generation time dramatically and hold slots longer.
- In Dedicated pools with heterogenous tenants, admission priority inversion occurs: long requests pin GPU resources while admission queues keep accepting new long-context requests due to backlog amplification.
- Private upgrade windows can trigger brief prefetch pauses that cause a cascade of long-request slowdowns, increasing suffocation duration.

Root cause hypothesis:
A combination of (1) missing admission expiry policy that treats admission tokens as indefinite for long-context requests, (2) admission accounting not decrementing when prefetch/eviction stalls extend generation beyond expected windows, and (3) lack of a weighted ageing mechanism to favour short, latency-sensitive flows during microbursts.

Mitigation implemented (hotfix v1):
- Short-term hotfix deployed to hosted API (runtime-1.19-hotfix): admission expiry added with conservative 10s soft timeout for pending generator slots; prefetch backoff applied when KV eviction probability crosses threshold.
- Canary rollouts to Dedicated customers who reported issues; toggles added behind feature-flag admit_timeout_v1.
- Private customer emergency guidance: disable prefetch or increase eviction hysteresis until runtime-1.20 patch is applied.

Work planned (this ticket):
1) Design and implement 'transparent admission expiry' (final) with weighted ageing and adaptive expiry based on observed sequence length distribution and tenant SLAs. Owner: Marco Chen. Due: 2026-03-18.
2) Add telemetry: per-tenant admission hold time histogram, admission-expiry-trigger reason codes, and KV-eviction correlation metrics. Owner: Sara Nguyen. Due: 2026-03-15.
3) Develop a simulation harness for mixed-length waves to validate fairness improvements under synthetic and recorded production traces. Owner: Julian Park. Estimate: 2 points.
4) Implement grace drain + backpressure signals for Private upgrade window operations so prefetch pauses do not convert to long admission holds. Owner: Lena Ortiz. Due: 2026-03-22.
5) Release plan: runtime-1.20 with opt-in weighted ageing and adaptive expiry; staged rollout across hosted, Dedicated, then Private. Rollback plan: feature-flag off + revert admission expiry to hotfix behavior.

Testing and validation strategy:
- Unit tests for admission lifetime accounting and weighted ageing rules.
- Load tests on perf-cluster with recorded production arrival traces (three customers). Must show p95 latency for short requests reduces to baseline +/-10% under mixed waves.
- Chaos test: induce KV-cache eviction spikes and prefetch pauses to validate adaptive expiry doesn’t create new starvation modes.

Monitoring & Alerts:
- New alert: AdmissionHoldMedian > 2s AND ShortRequestP95Increase > 30% for 5 minutes => Priority paging.
- Dashboards: Admission hold time heatmap, per-tenant backlog amplification ratio, kernel utilization vs admission-hold scatterplot. Links: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/adm/adm-hold (internal), https://dash.redwood.company/incident/INC-2026-0311 (incident dashboard).

Customer comms:
- Sent initial postmortem to impacted customers with workaround steps and ETA for final fix (Aisha Patel).
- Next update scheduled 2026-03-13 with planned runtime-1.20 rollout timeline.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Expiry aggressiveness: too aggressive expiry may cause wasted GPU cycles / partial generations; too lax preserves starvation. We will tune adaptively based on per-tenant SLAs and observed p50/p95 trade-offs.
- Weighted ageing complexity vs operator mental overhead: implement as server-side defaults with per-tenant overrides in Dedicated.

Related artifacts and links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9812 (admission-expiry prototype)
- Canary results: https://ci.redwood.company/canaries/22459 (internal)
- Incident ticket: INC-2026-0311
- Playbook update: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/INF/Admission+Expiry+Playbook

Acceptance criteria (for Done):
- Weighted admission-ageing merged and behind default-on feature flag in runtime-1.20.
- Perf tests show short-request p95 restored to baseline under mixed-length wave scenarios.
- Monitoring present and alerting configured; public-facing postmortem published for affected customers.

Postmortem notes (ongoing):
- Early indications from canary show p95 short-request latency drops by ~45% during synthetic mixed bursts when adaptive expiry is enabled.
- One Dedicated tenant showed increased token waste due to premature expiry on extremely long streams; mitigation: per-tenant SLA whitelist and adaptive window expansion.

Next steps (immediate):
- Complete telemetry patch and staged rollout plan (Sara + Marco) by 2026-03-15.
- Run full regression load tests by 2026-03-16.
- Schedule customer-facing postmortem and timeline email on 2026-03-18.
